contradictions: The site's operating legal entity is reported inconsistently across secondary sources: 'NovaForge Ltd', 'Santeda International B.V.', 'Casolinia Group' (Anjouan), 'Boomerang N.V./Boomerang Partners' (Curaçao), and 'Rabidi N.V.' (Curaçao) have each been attributed to BillyBets by different low-authority aggregator sites, with no single name corroborated against a primary source (T&Cs or company registry).

Claimed licensing jurisdiction varies by source: PAGCOR (Philippines), Anjouan, and Curaçao are all claimed in different places, plus one uncorroborated claim of a Malta Gaming Authority licence that could not be matched to any MGA register entry — suggesting either misattribution by review sites or shifting/multiple licence claims by the operator, a pattern consistent with regulatory-arbitrage behaviour documented elsewhere in this brand family (industry reporting describes the same white-label group cycling through licensee entities Rabidi N.V. -> Adonio N.V. -> Liernin Enterprises Ltd. and licences Curaçao(Antillephone) -> PAGCOR).

The target domain is named 'billybetsportugal.com' (apparently targeting Portuguese-speaking players) yet is the subject of a Spanish jurisdiction enforcement inquiry, consistent with the known industry pattern of country-specific mirror domains reaching players outside their nominal target market.

No DGOJ (Spain) authorisation was found for BillyBets or any of its candidate operating entities, while the wider brand network it is commercially associated with ('Boomerang Partners' family) has been explicitly reported by an independent investigation as classified unauthorised by Spanish authorities specifically.
analystNotes: This investigation was significantly constrained by a tool-level failure: the WebFetch capability returned HTTP 403 for every URL attempted in this session, including the target site (https://www.billybetsportugal.com and http://www.billybetsportugal.com), the likely parent brand (billybets.com, billybetscom.com), mirror/T&C pages (playbillybets.com/terms/, billybet-casinos.com/terms/), and even a neutral control URL (example.com) — indicating a systemic block on direct page retrieval in this environment rather than site-specific blocking alone. As a result, no page content (footer, T&Cs, licensing page, WHOIS record) could be directly read or quoted; all findings in this brief are derived from WebSearch result snippets and AI-generated summaries of those snippets, which are known to occasionally over-generalise or blend information from multiple unrelated sources. Consequently: (1) the operating legal entity, registration number, and registered address are all 'unknown' rather than asserted from any single named candidate, despite several candidate names surfacing in searches; (2) no licence reference numbers could be confirmed against PAGCOR, Anjouan, Curaçao, or MGA registers; (3) WHOIS data for the target domain could not be retrieved. The strongest, most defensible finding is the reputational/network one: BillyBets is commercially marketed alongside the 'Boomerang' brand via the 'Boomerang Partners' affiliate program, and Boomerang has been independently reported (Investigate Europe) as unauthorised in Spain among other countries — this is a solid investigative lead connecting the target brand's marketing network to documented illegal-in-Spain gambling operations, even though a direct, verified link from BillyBets to a specific licensed/incorporated entity was not achievable with the tools available. Recommend the enforcement team: (a) directly retrieve billybetsportugal.com's Terms & Conditions/Imprint from a non-blocked network path to identify the disclosed operating company; (b) run a formal WHOIS query outside this session; (c) query the DGOJ, PAGCOR, Anjouan Gaming Board and Curaçao Gaming Control Board registers directly for 'BillyBets' and each candidate entity name listed above.
